category: Schematic: Project Options tabs, ERC categories, annotation commands, hierarchy & harness placement
description: Project-level configuration (Project > Project Options tabs and the electrical rule check categories), the Tools > Annotation commands, hierarchy management commands (sheet symbols, device sheets, up/down hierarchy, net identifier scope) and signal-harness placement objects of the schematic editor.

tools.name: Project Options > General
tools.description: First tab of Project > Project Options: for Workspace (Altium 365) projects it controls online availability/synchronisation, version control binding, the server folder, conflict-prevention notifications and requirements linking; for local projects it shows the project path and type. Other tabs hold the compiler and output behaviour.
tools.usage: Project > Project Options... > General

parameters.name: Server folder / Version control
parameters.description: Workspace location and VCS binding for managed projects.

tools.example: Open Project Options, General tab, confirm the project is bound to the Workspace before enabling Design > Comments.
tools.notes: Project options are stored in the .PrjPcb file; templates can pre-set them.

tools.name: Project Options > Error Reporting
tools.description: Sets the report mode (No Report, Warning, Error, Fatal Error) for every electrical and drafting check performed by Project > Validate PCB Project, grouped as Violations Associated with Buses, Components, Documents, Harnesses, Nets, Others and Parameters. Results appear in the Messages panel; Fatal Errors block ECO generation.
tools.usage: Project > Project Options... > Error Reporting (right-click for All Off / All Warning / All Error / All Fatal / Default)

parameters.name: Report Mode
parameters.description: No Report | Warning | Error | Fatal Error per violation type.

tools.example: Raise 'Floating Net Labels' and 'Nets with only one pin' to Error before release so they cannot be ignored.
tools.notes: Suppress individual instances with a No ERC directive rather than lowering the global level.

tools.name: ERC: Violations Associated with Nets
tools.description: Net-level checks: Adding hidden net to sheet, Adding items from hidden net, Auto-assigned ports to device pins, Duplicate nets, Floating net labels, Floating power objects, Global power-objects scope changes, Net parameters with no name/value, Nets containing floating input pins, Nets containing multiple similar objects, Nets with multiple names, Nets with no driving source, Nets with only one pin, Nets with possible connection problems, Same net used in multiple differential pairs, Sheets containing duplicate ports, Signals with multiple drivers, Signals with no driver, Signals with no load, Unconnected objects in net, Unconnected wires.
tools.usage: Project Options > Error Reporting > Violations Associated with Nets
tools.example: Typical settings: Floating net labels = Error, Nets with only one pin = Warning, Nets with multiple names = Error, Unconnected wires = Error.
tools.notes: 'Nets with no driving source' depends on pin electrical types (Output/Power vs Input) set in the symbol.

tools.name: ERC: Violations Associated with Components
tools.description: Component checks: Component Implementations with duplicate pins used / invalid pin / missing pins / standard pin, Components containing duplicate sub-parts, Components with duplicate pins, Duplicate Component Designators (usually Error), Duplicate Part Designators, Extra pin found in component display mode, Mismatched hidden pin connections, Mismatched pin visibility, Missing component models / model parameters / pin in sequence, Unused sub-part in component, Un-Designated parts requiring annotation, plus 'Component revision is out of date' and 'Component revision has inapplicable state' for managed components.
tools.usage: Project Options > Error Reporting > Violations Associated with Components
tools.example: Set Duplicate Component Designators = Fatal Error and Un-Designated parts requiring annotation = Error to force annotation before ECO.
tools.notes: Managed-component revision checks are also surfaced by the Item Manager.

tools.name: ERC: Violations Associated with Documents and Others
tools.description: Document checks: Conflicting Constraints, Duplicate sheet numbers, Duplicate sheet symbol names, Missing child sheet for sheet symbol, Missing Configuration Target, Missing sub-project sheet for component, Multiple configuration targets, Multiple Top-Level Documents, Port not linked to parent sheet symbol, Sheet entry not linked to child sheet, Sheet symbol with duplicate entries, Unique identifiers errors. Others: Fail to add alternate item, Incorrect link in project variant, Object not completely within sheet boundaries, Off-grid object.
tools.usage: Project Options > Error Reporting > Violations Associated with Documents / Others
tools.example: Off-grid object = Warning helps catch components dragged off the 100 mil grid; Multiple Top-Level Documents = Error catches an orphaned sheet.
tools.notes: Unique identifier errors (duplicate UIDs after copying parts between projects) are fixed from the Messages panel, whose right-click menu offers to reset the component unique IDs.

tools.name: ERC: Violations Associated with Buses, Harnesses and Parameters
tools.description: Bus checks: Arbiter/Bus index out of range, Bus range syntax errors, Illegal bus range values, Illegal bus definitions, Mismatched bus label ordering, Mismatched bus/wire object on wire/bus, Mismatched bus widths, Mismatched bus section index ordering, Mismatched electrical types on bus, Mismatched generics on bus, Mixed generic and numeric bus labeling. Harness checks: Conflicting harness definition, Harness connector type syntax error, Missing harness type on harness, Multiple harness types on harness, Unknown harness type. Parameter checks: Same parameter containing different types, Same parameter containing different values.
tools.usage: Project Options > Error Reporting > Violations Associated with Buses / Harnesses / Parameters
tools.example: Mismatched bus widths = Error catches D[0..7] wired to a D[0..15] port.
tools.notes: Harness definition conflicts often come from stale .Harness files; delete them and recompile.

tools.name: Project Options > Connection Matrix
tools.description: Matrix of pin electrical types and net identifiers (Input, I/O, Output, Open Collector, Passive, HiZ, Open Emitter, Power pins; Input/Output/Bidirectional/Unspecified ports and sheet entries; Unconnected) where each cell's colour sets how a connection between the two kinds is reported: green No Report, yellow Warning, orange Error, red Fatal Error. Click cells to cycle. This is where 'Output pin connected to Output pin' or 'Unconnected input pin' severities are defined.
tools.usage: Project > Project Options... > Connection Matrix (click a cell to cycle severity; right-click for presets)

parameters.name: Cell severity
parameters.description: No Report | Warning | Error | Fatal Error for each pin/port pair.

tools.example: Set Input Pin vs Unconnected to Error so every floating input must be tied off or marked with a No ERC directive.
tools.notes: Correct pin electrical types in symbols are prerequisite; many library parts use Passive for everything, which defeats the matrix.

tools.name: Project Options > Class Generation
tools.description: Controls which classes are created automatically when the design is transferred to the PCB: net classes for buses, named signal harnesses and bus sections; component classes and net classes per schematic sheet (Generate Component Classes / Net Classes for sheet, with Create Rooms option); structure classes; plus user-defined classes from directives. Options interact with the Comparator and ECO Generation tabs.
tools.usage: Project > Project Options... > Class Generation

parameters.name: Component Classes / Net Classes per sheet
Generate Net Classes for Buses / Named Harnesses / Bus Sections

tools.example: Enable Component Classes per sheet with Create Rooms so each schematic sheet becomes a room on the PCB for grouped placement.
tools.notes: Disable rooms per sheet on small boards to avoid room-confinement DRC noise.

tools.name: Project Options > Comparator
tools.description: Defines which differences between schematic and PCB are found or ignored (Find Differences / Ignore Differences) for object types: components, nets, net classes, component classes, rooms, differential pairs, structure classes, parameters, footprints, rules from directives, and how objects are matched (by unique ID, designator, name). Extra classes/rooms present only on the PCB are kept when set to Ignore.
tools.usage: Project > Project Options... > Comparator

parameters.name: Object Matching Criteria
parameters.description: Min/Max match percentage for nets/classes and parameter matching.

tools.example: Set Extra Net Classes and Extra Component Classes to Ignore Differences so PCB-side classes survive Design > Update PCB.
tools.notes: Comparator results feed the ECO; changes in Comparator without matching ECO Generation settings produce no change orders.

tools.name: Project Options > ECO Generation
tools.description: Chooses which modification types produce Engineering Change Orders (Generate Change Orders / Ignore) grouped by Components, Nets, Parameters, Classes, Rooms, Differential pairs, Structure classes, Rules: e.g. Add/Remove Components, Change Component Footprints/Parameters, Add/Remove Nets, Add/Remove Net Classes, Change Room Definitions. Used to stop specific changes (like removing PCB-only nets) from being pushed.
tools.usage: Project > Project Options... > ECO Generation
tools.example: Set Remove Net Classes = Ignore and Remove Rooms = Ignore to protect hand-made PCB classes and rooms.
tools.notes: Pair with Comparator settings; the ECO dialog also allows unticking individual changes each time.

tools.name: Project Options > Options (output path, ECO log, net identifier scope)
tools.description: Miscellaneous compiler and output options: Output Path and ECO Log Path (with Use separate folder for each output type), Output Options (Open outputs after compile, Timestamp folder, Archive project on compile), Netlist Options (Allow Ports/Sheet Entries to Name Nets, Append Sheet Numbers to Local Nets, Higher Level Names Take Priority, Power Port Names Take Priority), Net Identifier Scope (Automatic, Flat, Hierarchical, Strict Hierarchical, Global) and Allow Pin-Swapping Using These Methods (Adding/Removing Net-Labels, Changing Schematic Pins).
tools.usage: Project > Project Options... > Options

parameters.name: Net Identifier Scope
parameters.description: Automatic (Based on source) | Flat (Only ports global) | Hierarchical (Sheet entry <-> port) | Strict Hierarchical | Global (Net labels and ports global).

parameters.name: Output Path
parameters.description: Folder for generated outputs (default Project Outputs for <project>).

tools.example: Set Net Identifier Scope = Hierarchical and enable Allow Ports to Name Nets so top-level port names become PCB net names.
tools.notes: Changing scope on an existing design can rename many nets; check with Project > Show Differences.

tools.name: Project Options > Multi-Channel
tools.description: Naming for multi-channel designs: Room Naming Style (Flat Numeric / Flat Alpha / Hierarchical Numeric / Hierarchical Alpha with room level separator) and Component Designator Format using $Component, $ChannelIndex, $ChannelAlpha, $RoomName, $ComponentIndex tokens (e.g. $Component_$ChannelIndex or $Component$ChannelAlpha). The format decides the PCB designators of repeated channels.
tools.usage: Project > Project Options... > Multi-Channel
tools.example: Format $Component_$ChannelIndex gives R1_1, R1_2... for Repeat(AMP,1,4); then Board Level Annotate to assign flat designators.
tools.notes: Rooms per channel are created when Class Generation rooms are enabled.

tools.name: Project Options > Default Prints
tools.description: Lists every output type (Assembly, Documentation, Fabrication, Other, Report, Validation categories) with a Print checkbox and Configure button to define which outputs are produced by the legacy File > Print Project / Default Prints mechanism when no OutJob is used.
tools.usage: Project > Project Options... > Default Prints
tools.example: Tick Schematic Prints and PCB Prints, Configure PCB Prints to a top-assembly layer set, then File > Default Prints.
tools.notes: Output Job files are the modern replacement and are recommended for repeatable outputs.

tools.name: Project Options > Search Paths
tools.description: Ordered folders searched for libraries and models (STEP, SPICE, IBIS) when resolving links, each with a file filter and Include Sub-Folders flag. Hidden by default in AD20.2.3+ until UI.ProjectOptions.SearchPaths is enabled in Advanced Settings; Preferences > Data Management > File-based Libraries offers the global equivalent.
tools.usage: Project > Project Options... > Search Paths (requires UI.ProjectOptions.SearchPaths advanced setting)
tools.example: Add ..\Models\STEP with filter *.step and sub-folders so footprints find STEP bodies by file name.
tools.notes: Relative paths are resolved from the project folder, which keeps projects portable.

tools.name: Project Options > Parameters
tools.description: Project-level parameters (name/value) available on every sheet and PCB as special strings (=ParameterName), for title-block fields such as Revision, Author, Customer, ProjectName. Parameters from a project template arrive here; the Parameter Manager can also edit them.
tools.usage: Project > Project Options... > Parameters > Add
tools.example: Add Revision = B; place the special string =Revision in the sheet template title block and in the PCB silkscreen.
tools.notes: Document parameters (Document Options) override project parameters of the same name.

tools.name: Project Options > Device Sheets / Managed OutputJobs / Library Options
tools.description: Device Sheets tab: folders (with processing order) that contain reusable device sheets referenced by Device Sheet Symbols; Managed OutputJobs: Workspace OutJob templates made available to the project for release; Library Options: chooses the integrated-library format used when compiling from this project (Original or Altium Designer).
tools.usage: Project > Project Options... > Device Sheets | Managed OutputJobs | Library Options
tools.example: Add the corporate 'DeviceSheets\Power' folder, then Place > Device Sheet Symbol lists its sheets.
tools.notes: Device sheet folders can also be set globally in Preferences > Data Management > Device Sheets.

tools.name: Tools > Annotation > Annotate Schematics Quietly
tools.description: Assigns unique designators to every un-designated component (R?, C?) across all annotation-enabled sheets using the last settings of the Annotate dialog, without opening it; already-designated parts are untouched. The fastest way to annotate during rapid capture before validating the project.
tools.usage: Tools > Annotation > Annotate Schematics Quietly (T A Q)
tools.example: Place ten parts, press T A Q, then Project > Validate PCB Project.
tools.notes: Use Tools > Annotation > Annotate Schematics (full dialog) to change order, start index or per-sheet ranges.

tools.name: Tools > Annotation > Number Schematic Sheets
tools.description: Opens Sheet Numbering For Project to assign SheetNumber, DocumentNumber and SheetTotal parameters to each schematic in logical/physical order (Auto Sheet Number, Auto Document Number, Update Sheet Count), which the special strings =SheetNumber, =DocumentNumber and =SheetTotal display in title blocks.
tools.usage: Tools > Annotation > Number Schematic Sheets...

parameters.name: Auto Sheet Number / Auto Document Number / Update Sheet Count

tools.example: Reorder sheets in the Projects panel, run Number Schematic Sheets > Auto Sheet Number > Update Sheet Count, then check the title blocks show 3 of 12.
tools.notes: Compiled (physical) sheet instances of multi-channel designs are numbered with Annotate Compiled Sheets instead.

tools.name: Tools > Annotation > Reset Schematic Designators
tools.description: Resets every designator on the annotation-enabled sheets of the project back to its undesignated form (R?, U?), except locked designators, so the design can be renumbered from scratch with a new annotation order. Reset Duplicate Schematic Designators only resets duplicates.
tools.usage: Tools > Annotation > Reset Schematic Designators | Reset Duplicate Schematic Designators
tools.example: Reset Schematic Designators, then Annotate Schematics with 'Down Then Across' order and start index 1 per sheet.
tools.notes: Resetting breaks the PCB link until an ECO with matching unique IDs is run; back up first.

tools.name: Tools > Annotation > Annotate Compiled Sheets
tools.description: Numbers the physical (compiled) instances of sheets in multi-channel designs, assigning each channel instance its own sheet number so printed compiled output is unambiguous; complements Number Schematic Sheets which numbers logical sheets.
tools.usage: Tools > Annotation > Annotate Compiled Sheets...
tools.example: After Repeat(CH,1,8), run Annotate Compiled Sheets so the eight channel instances print as sheets 5-12.
tools.notes: Requires a compiled project (Project > Validate PCB Project).

tools.name: Design > Create Sheet Symbol From Sheet / Create Sheet From Sheet Symbol
tools.description: Hierarchy helpers: Create Sheet Symbol From Sheet builds a sheet symbol (with sheet entries matching the ports) for an existing schematic and lets you place it on the parent; Create Sheet From Sheet Symbol generates a new child sheet whose ports match the entries of a placed symbol. Design > Synchronize Sheet Entries and Ports keeps them aligned afterwards.
tools.usage: Design > Create Sheet Symbol From Sheet | Create Sheet From Sheet Symbol | Synchronize Sheet Entries and Ports
tools.example: Draw PSU.SchDoc with ports VIN, VOUT, GND; on Top.SchDoc run Design > Create Sheet Symbol From Sheet, pick PSU.SchDoc, place the symbol.
tools.notes: Sheet entries and ports must match in name and I/O type for hierarchical connectivity.

tools.name: Tools > Up/Down Hierarchy
tools.description: Navigates the design hierarchy: click a sheet symbol/sheet entry to open the child sheet (zoomed to the matching port), or a port to jump up to the parent's sheet entry. Also available via Ctrl+double-click on a sheet symbol and from the Navigator panel.
tools.usage: Tools > Up/Down Hierarchy (T H), then click a sheet symbol, sheet entry or port
tools.example: T H, click the 'VOUT' sheet entry: the PSU sheet opens centred on the VOUT port.
tools.notes: Requires a validated project for cross-sheet navigation to be accurate.

tools.name: Hierarchical vs flat design (net identifier scope)
tools.description: Altium supports flat designs (all sheets at one level, connected by global ports or net labels) and hierarchical designs (parent sheets with sheet symbols whose entries connect to child ports), decided by the Net Identifier Scope option. Hierarchical/Strict Hierarchical is recommended for reuse and multi-channel; Flat uses ports globally; Global makes net labels project-wide; Automatic picks based on the presence of sheet symbols and ports.
tools.usage: Project Options > Options > Net Identifier Scope; structure shown in the Projects panel (Structure view) and Navigator
tools.example: Top.SchDoc contains sheet symbols for MCU, PSU, IO; each child exposes ports; scope Hierarchical; buses cross via sheet entries D[0..7].
tools.notes: Off-sheet connectors are a flat-design object; ports in hierarchical mode connect only to their parent's entries.

tools.name: Place > Device Sheet Symbol
tools.description: Places a sheet symbol that references a read-only device sheet (a reusable, centrally stored circuit block) from the folders configured in Project Options or Preferences > Data Management > Device Sheets; the entries are created from the device sheet's ports. Device sheets stay read-only unless the read-only option is cleared in the Device Sheets preferences, and their components are annotated with Board Level Annotation.
tools.usage: Place > Device Sheet Symbol (choose from the device sheet list)

parameters.name: Device sheet
parameters.description: Sheet chosen from configured device-sheet folders.

tools.example: Place > Device Sheet Symbol > 'USB_ESD_Protection', wire its D+/D- entries; designators are assigned at board level.
tools.notes: Device sheets are watermarked and locked by default (Preferences > Data Management > Device Sheets).

tools.name: Place > Harness > Signal Harness
tools.description: Draws a signal harness line, a single graphical connection that bundles several nets/buses (defined by a harness type) between harness connectors, sheet entries and ports of type Harness. Harness lines are placed like buses (Place > Harness > Signal Harness, P H H) with the same corner modes.
tools.usage: Place > Harness > Signal Harness (P H H)
tools.example: Place a Harness Connector 'SPI' with entries MOSI, MISO, SCK, CS, then a Signal Harness from its neck to a sheet entry of harness type SPI on the MCU sheet symbol.
tools.notes: The compiler writes a .Harness definition file per harness type into the project folder.

tools.name: Place > Harness > Harness Connector
tools.description: Places the harness connector object: a box with a Harness Type field (e.g. 'SPI') and a neck point where the signal harness attaches; wires, buses or other harnesses enter through Harness Entries on its edge. Properties: Harness Type, size, colours, and the entries list.
tools.usage: Place > Harness > Harness Connector (P H C); Tab to set Harness Type

parameters.name: Harness Type
parameters.description: Name that ties this connector to sheet entries/ports of the same type.

tools.example: Place Harness Connector, Tab, Harness Type 'I2C', place; add entries SDA, SCL.
tools.notes: Harness connectors on sheet symbols are created automatically when a sheet entry is set to Harness type.

tools.name: Place > Harness > Harness Entry
tools.description: Places a named entry on the edge of a harness connector; each entry names a signal (net), bus (e.g. D[0..7]) or nested harness carried by the harness, and wires/buses are connected to it. Entries define the harness type's contents.
tools.usage: Place > Harness > Harness Entry (P H E); hover the connector edge and click; Tab to name

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Signal, bus or nested harness name.

tools.example: Add entries 'SDA' and 'SCL' to the I2C connector and wire them to the sensor pins.
tools.notes: Mismatched entry sets for the same harness type across sheets raise 'Conflicting harness definition' violations.

tools.name: Tools > Item Manager
tools.description: Dialog that maps placed components (from file libraries, database libraries or older managed items) to Workspace managed components, showing the current source and proposed Item/revision for each designator; Apply ECO replaces the links project-wide. Also used to update components to their latest revisions and to migrate legacy designs to managed content.
tools.usage: Tools > Item Manager...

parameters.name: Match / Set Item
parameters.description: Automatic or manual mapping to Workspace items.

parameters.name: ECO
parameters.description: Generates change orders to relink components.

tools.example: Open Item Manager, select all rows, Choose Latest Revision, click ECO, Execute Changes.
tools.notes: Requires a connected Workspace; the Components panel's 'Update to latest revision' is a per-part alternative.

tools.name: Design > Document Options (Properties panel sheet settings)
tools.description: With nothing selected the Properties panel shows document options: General (Units mm/mil, Visible Grid, Snap Grid, Snap to Electrical Object Hotspots with range, Document font), Page Options (Template, or Standard sheet size A4-A0/Letter..., or Custom, orientation, Title Block, Margins, Zones), Parameters (document-level parameters) and Sheet Colours. Templates are applied here or via Design > Templates.
tools.usage: Click empty sheet area > Properties panel; or Design > Document Options
tools.example: Set Page Options to Template 'A3_Company.SchDot' and add parameter DrawnBy = J. Doe.
tools.notes: Use Design > Templates > Update Template on all sheets after editing the template file.

tools.name: Design > Templates (sheet template commands)
tools.description: Sub-menu for schematic templates: General Templates (apply a .SchDot to the current sheet, all sheets or project), Update Template (re-apply the template and optionally update parameters) and Remove Current Template; templates themselves are created with File > Save As using the Advanced Schematic template (*.SchDot) type. Templates hold the sheet border, title block graphics and default parameters.
tools.usage: Design > Templates > General Templates... | Update Template... | Remove Current Template

parameters.name: Scope
parameters.description: Just this document / All schematic documents in the project / All open documents.

parameters.name: Parameter actions
parameters.description: Do not update / Add new only / Replace all.

tools.example: Design > Templates > Update Template, choose 'All schematic documents in the current project', parameter action 'Add new parameters that exist in template only'.
tools.notes: Templates can be managed in the Workspace (Preferences > Data Management > Templates).

tools.name: Design > Make Schematic Library
tools.description: Creates a project schematic library (.SchLib) containing every symbol placed in the project's schematics (including their model links), for archiving the exact symbols used or for editing symbols locally. The schematic counterpart of Design > Make PCB Library.
tools.usage: Design > Make Schematic Library (schematic editor)
tools.example: Design > Make Schematic Library, save 'Board_Symbols.SchLib', then edit a pin and use Tools > Update Schematics from the library editor.
tools.notes: Design > Make Integrated Library builds the .IntLib from the same data.

tools.name: Project > Variants (fitted / not fitted / alternate part)
tools.description: The Variant Management dialog (Project > Variants) defines assembly variants where each component is Fitted, Not Fitted or replaced by an Alternate Part (a different component with its own parameters); variant-specific parameter values are also allowed. Outputs (BOM, assembly drawings, pick and place, PCB 3D) are generated per variant from the OutJob; the schematic shows variant state via crossed-out symbols when a variant is selected.
tools.usage: Project > Variants... (add variant, set component options); select the active variant from the toolbar or Projects panel
tools.example: Create variant 'LowCost': set U5 Not Fitted, R12 Alternate Part 10k; OutJob BOM with Variant = LowCost.
tools.notes: Variants are stored in the .PrjPcb; the PCB's Variant selector controls 3D/assembly views.

tools.name: Project > Validate PCB Project (compiler run)
tools.description: Compiles the project: builds the hierarchy, generates nets and classes, runs the electrical rule checks per Error Reporting and Connection Matrix, and populates the Messages and Navigator panels. Must succeed (no Fatal Errors) before Design > Update PCB Document can create an ECO. Formerly 'Compile PCB Project'.
tools.usage: Project > Validate PCB Project <name>; or right-click the project in the Projects panel > Validate PCB Project
tools.example: Validate, double-click an 'Unconnected wire' message to jump to it, fix, validate again.
tools.notes: Auto-compile on Update PCB is enabled by default; use Compile Masks to exclude blocks under construction.
